pulls.title: RISC-V: Make float16ToFloat ignore upper argument bits
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi ,please consider. this patch fix the RISC-V implementation of `Float.float16ToFloat` when the incoming short argument has non-normalized upper bits. The JVM verifier represents short values as integers on the operand stack. Therefore, valid bytecode may invoke `float16ToFloat(short)` without first sign-extending the low 16 bits. The RISC-V NaN/infinity slow path previously shifted the complete source register and assumed that it was already sign-extended. pulls.author: vpelikh
pulls.body_excerpt: ## Problem A Vector API value passed as an argument to a method that C2 does **not** inline is materialized on the heap at the call site. A method that applies a sequence of Vector API operations (no loops, just one operation after another) is large by construction: each operation is a separate call in the bytecode, so a method with a dozen of them easily exceeds `FreqInlineSize` (325 bytes by default). pulls.title: 8393264: SplashDecodeGif may read past colour table
pulls.author: Sovtouch
pulls.body_excerpt: SplashDecodeGif() uses gif->SBackGroundColor as an index into colorMap->Colors when handling GIF_DISPOSE_BACKGND. The background colour index is read from the GIF Logical Screen Descriptor and may contain a value from 0 to 255. The value is not validated against colorMap->ColorCount before indexing the colour table. A malformed GIF with a small colour table and an out-of-range SBackGroundColor can therefore cause an out-of-bounds heap read. pulls.title: 8390358: HotCodeCollector can relocate never-sampled nmethod
pulls.author: eastig
pulls.body_excerpt: HotCodeCollector stores `nmethod*` pointers during sampling. Code blobs can be freed and reused for other nmethods in between sampling and relocation. As a result we can relocate never-sampled nmethod. I managed to create a test which reproduces the issue. However the test is not reliable to be added to jtreg tests. It depends on a host and OS is being run on. To avoid the issue, I use compile ids to distinguish nmethods. We need to dereference nmethod pointer during sampling without holding locks. pulls.title: 8393085: AArch64: implement compact uncommon trap sequence
pulls.author: ruben-arm
pulls.body_excerpt: Prior to this change, uncommon trap sequences in C2 were implemented as static Java calls - involving unnecessary spilling and post-call NOPs. Introduce MachUncommonTrapNode. The node represents transition to the uncommon trap blob. It is a safepoint, however - unlike static Java calls - it does not require spilling of values from registers, because all values are preserved by the uncommon trap blob at the entry point. Also, no post-call NOP sequence is emitted for the node. These differences substantially reduce size of C2-compiled methods. The sequence consists of a BL followed by int32 trap

pulls.title: 8346177: C2: optimize simple increment loops with loop-invariant strides
pulls.author: krk
pulls.body_excerpt: The old `replace_parallel_iv` only optimized parallel IVs with constant increments that evenly divided the primary IV's stride. Patterns like `a += field` or `a += param` where the increment is loop-invariant but not a compile-time constant were left as accumulation loops. This patch generalizes the optimization to accept any loop-invariant increment, adds subtraction support, and removes the exact-divisibility requirement. Instead of computing a ratio between strides, the iteration count is computed directly as `(iv - init) / stride_con`. A simple benchmark `for (i=0; i<100000; i++) a += inc`
